import React from 'react'

import { Button } from '@rtm-ui/button';
import { DummyComponent } from './dummy-component';

};

    super(props)

    const { components, ...props } = this.props

reporting`}</MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="li" components={components} parentName="ul">{`Providing an error boundary. If any `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="li">{`children`}</MDXTag>{` throw an error, the Bootstrap
component will catch it, log it, and show the user an appropriate message.`}</MDXTag>
</MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="p" components={components}>{`There will likely be more responsibilities in the future. In general, the
Bootstrap package handles setup and should be the single source of truth
for most "global" needs for a given app.`}</MDXTag>
<MDXTag name="blockquote" components={components}>
<MDXTag name="p" components={components} parentName="blockquote">{`Note: the error handling at this level is extremely minimal as it's the last
possible opportunity to catch an error before the app is entirely unmounted from the
DOM. As a general rule, you should be wrapping most higher-level components (ex. `}<MDXTag name="inlineCode" components={components} parentName="p">{`@rtm-ui/plan`}</MDXTag>{`)

</MDXTag>
